newsitem.title: USA: Host Marriott EBITDA up 42 pct, revs 51 pct.
newsitem.headline: Host Marriott EBITDA up 42 pct, revs 51 pct.

text.p: Host Marriott Corp said Monday preliminary 1996 EBITDA -- Earnings Before Interest Expense, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization, and other non-cash items -- were about $442 million, a 42 percent increase over its 1995 results of $311 million.
Revenues for the year are expected to have increased by about 51 percent to $732 million from $484 million in 1995, it said.
Host Marriott said full service hotel EBITDA for the year increased to $415 million, a 68 percent improvement from $247 million in 1995.

The full service hotel EBITDA increase in 1996 is attributable primarily to a 19 percent increase in comparable hotel EBITDA on an 11 percent increase in room revenue per available room, as well as incremental EBITDA generated by the company's 1996 and 1995 hotel acquisitions, the company said.

For the 1996 fourth quarter, the company also said comparable hotel EBITDA increased 21 percent on a 10 percent increase in revenue per room over the 1995 fourth quarter. Full year and fourth quarter results for 1996 also include 53 and 17 weeks, respectively, versus 52 and 16 weeks, respectively, included in the comparable 1995 periods.

This put fourth quarter revenues at $268 million, up from $165 million in 1995, while EBITDA rose to $159 million from $99 million. The company said it will report fiscal year 1996 results of operations in early March.

In remarks prepared for an investor conference, chief executive Terence C. Golden said, "We are extraordinarily pleased with the financial results we are seeing for 1996. The growth in hotel EBITDA reflects the impact of our 1995 and 1996 hotel acquisitions and the continuing strength of the full service sector of the hotel industry in which we are focused."

Golden continued, "Through our aggressive acquisition program, Host Marriott was able to acquire, or purchase controlling interest in, 23 hotels (10,881 rooms) in 1996 with an aggregate value of approximately $1.5 billion.
"We have already acquired, or purchased controlling interest in, three additional hotels (2,433 rooms) in 1997 with an aggregate value of approximately $380 million."
Golden added, "With a 1997 acquisition target of over $1 billion, we expect to be able to continue to add high-quality, full-service hotels to our portfolio at attractive returns throughout 1997."
